Given the triangle above, find the length of $\overset{―}{AB}$ rounded to one decimal place.
question.worked_solution:
For an angle $\theta $ in a right triangle, the trigonometric ratios are as follows:

- $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$

- $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{adjacent leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$

- $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{adjacent leg}}$

First, note that we are given the length of the hypotenuse $\overset{―}{AC}$ and wish to find the length of the leg $\overset{―}{AB}$ opposite the given angle $∠C.$

The trigonometric ratio that relates the opposite leg to the hypotenuse is *sine*. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(m∠C) & =\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡({52}^{∘}) & =\frac{AB}{15} \\ AB & =15\operatorname{sin}⁡({52}^{∘}).\end{aligned}
$$

Using a calculator to evaluate the trigonometric ratio, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =15\operatorname{sin}⁡({52}^{∘}) \\  & =15(0.788\,01…) \\  & =11.820\,16… \\  & ≈11.8,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to one decimal place.
